column1: # Recorded body-size ceilings, in approximate tokens (whole-file chars/4,
# the same proxy scripts/custodian-skill-lint.sh reports).
# WHY THIS EXISTS. The lint reports the ~5000-token body budget as INFO,
# and 5000 is not reachable for a spec governing a five-phase unattended
# cron — so the advisory is permanently red and permanently ignored,
# which is recall rather than enforcement. These ceilings are the
# enforcement half: not the budget, but the size this file was LAST
# DELIBERATELY AGREED to be.
# THIS IS NOT A ONE-WAY RATCHET. A genuinely new mechanism is allowed to
# raise its ceiling — looper-custodian's body grew 646 tokens for the
# Phase A receipts sweep, and that growth paid for itself. What is not
# allowed is growing without anyone deciding. Raise the number in the
# same commit that grows the file, and the diff shows the trade.
# THE MARGIN IS DERIVED, NOT ROUND. A ceiling set to the file's exact
# size fails on the next sentence anyone writes, which trains people to
# raise the number reflexively — the opposite of a deliberate decision.
# So each ceiling carries roughly one mechanism's worth of slack, priced
# from the last real one: the Phase A receipts sweep cost 646 tokens for
# its paragraph, report line, roster entry and does-NOT line. One
# ordinary addition fits; a second forces the extract-or-raise call.
# Opt-in: a skill with no row here is not checked.
# skill
looper-custodian
column3: 8041 actual, 650 under; the ceiling is 8041 + ~650 for one mechanism, priced off the receipts sweep; the report body's rendering detail took it from 9667
